newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU threatens court action over mad cow measures.
newsitem.headline: EU threatens court action over mad cow measures.

text.p: The European Commission will take member states to court if, because of the mad cow disease crisis, they adopt unilateral trade measures that break the European Union's single market rules, a Commission spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman was commenting after France announced on Thursday an import ban on products from member states which did not remove suspect sheep and cattle tissue.
Spain has banned the import of meat and bonemeal feed and there is a ban on British dairy products in Germany.

But EU officials said ironically it could be Britain, which is banned from exporting its beef and beef products because of the didease, that is the first to be taken to court over its ban on the import of cattle over 30 months old.

"While we will strive to reach a political settlement we are concerned about the proliferation of unilateral action being taken by different member states relating to BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy)," said spokesman Gerard Kiely.
Kiely told a news briefing that EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler had warned of the danger to the single market at the start of the crisis in March.
If a political agreement proves impossible then the Commission will have no hesitation in going to the European Court of Justice, he said.
The Commission is compiling a dossier on infringements notably in France and Germany, Kiely added.
EU single market rules allow member states to adopt higher standards for their own products but forbids national bans on other states' products.
France had not informed the Commission of its unilateral measures but they appeared to be in line with Fischler's thinking, Kiely said.
"This is being discussed by the standing veterinary committee at the moment. Meanwhile we cannot have individual member states going their own way on such matters," he added.
